summary:
All 11 review-request scenarios pass on mobile web preview (390x844) — auto-strip Markdown fences on paste AND the Why?/Explain output → Apply Fix novice flow are fully functional. VERIFIED (paste): single-fence ```python
print('hello_paste')
``` collapses to just print('hello_paste') with paste-toast '[Fences stripped]'; no-fence content is left byte-for-byte unchanged and no toast fires; two consecutive ```ts blocks concatenate to 'const a = 1;

const b = 2;'; prose+fence input drops the prose and keeps only 'const x = 42;'; unbalanced 'x = ```foo…' has fence markers removed and does NOT crash the editor. VERIFIED (Why?): with 'prin("typo")' the console shows a NameError stderr, why-btn renders next to trash icon with icon alert-triangle and label 'Why?', tapping it router.push('/ai'), the auto-sent user message contains the '```python…```' fenced code block AND the 'STDERR:' block AND the 'You are a patient, beginner-friendly tutor' framing. VERIFIED (Apply Fix): after Gemini 3 Pro streams the response (took ~4-10s, EMERGENT_LLM_KEY working), the FIRST code block of the assistant reply shows all three buttons apply-fix-btn / insert-code-btn / copy-code-btn; tapping apply-fix-btn navigates back to / and REPLACES the editor content with the fenced code (defensive strip of any remaining ```lang…``` also confirmed via synthetic pending_replace path — a '```python
print("fixed")
```' value in AsyncStorage becomes just 'print("fixed")' in the editor), and paste-toast 'Fences stripped' fires immediately on return. VERIFIED (output-only variant): 'print("no error just output")' → stdout only, why-btn switches to icon 'help-circle' with label 'Explain output' (not 'Why?'). VERIFIED (regressions): Push modal opens with push-tab-github / push-tab-webhook / push-tab-share tabs and all form fields; long-press on filename-lang-picker opens Command Palette (runs 'Run current file' item); single tap on filename opens LangMenu (lang-menu); ⌘S / Ctrl+S triggers 'Saved' toast. No React Native red screens, no new deprecation warnings introduced by this feature set. Two pre-existing RN-Web deprecation nits from prior iterations still fire (shadow* → boxShadow; pointerEvents prop → style.pointerEvents on paste-toast wrapper); noted but out-of-scope.

react_native_issues.issue: RN-Web deprecation carried over from iteration 10: <View pointerEvents="none"> on the new paste-toast wrapper should use style.pointerEvents. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:1115

Existing RN-Web deprecation on savedToast style — the new paste-toast reuses styles.savedToast (with shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/shadowOffset) so it inherits the same warning. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:1346-1362

action_items: OPTIONAL polish (not blocking): dismiss the Console BottomSheetModal when the user taps why-btn — currently the sheet remains 'presented' behind the /ai screen. On web Expo Router keeps the sheet portal in the DOM so it stays visually docked at the bottom while the AI is chatting; harmless (Apply Fix / Insert / Copy still work) but slightly noisy UX. Consider calling `runSheetRef.current?.dismiss()` right before `router.push('/ai')` inside askAiAboutOutput.

Nit (carried from iter 10): migrate `shadow*` styles → `boxShadow` and `pointerEvents` prop → `style.pointerEvents` on styles.savedToast / the paste-toast wrapper in app/index.tsx to silence RN-Web deprecation warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: stripMarkdownFences() is well-scoped and defensive: it fast-returns when '```' isn't present, joins multi-block content with a blank line, and falls back to a regex-strip for unbalanced/stray fences — matches all 5 spec cases. The regex '```(?:[a-zA-Z][\w+\-.]*)?[ \t]*\r?\n?([\s\S]*?)\r?\n?```' correctly handles CRLF and lang labels like 'typescript+react'.

handleCodeChange gates the strip on `next.length - prevLen > 5 && next.includes('```')` — good heuristic: keeps single-char keystrokes fast and only triggers the (regex-heavy) strip on paste-like diffs.

Apply Fix flow is well-designed: the useFocusEffect on / prioritises pending_replace over pending_insert, defensively re-strips remaining fences, and updates prevContentLenRef.current so the next keystroke won't be misclassified as a paste. This is the correct pattern.

MessageBubble.firstCodeIdx correctly restricts Apply Fix to only the FIRST code block of an assistant reply, so multi-fence teaching responses don't render multiple Apply Fix buttons — matches the spec.

AI system prompt in askAiAboutOutput is well-shaped: language tag, code cap at 4000 chars, terminal-output cap at 4000 chars, explicit instruction to return the full corrected file inside a single fenced block with no prose. Gemini 3 Pro complied consistently across two live runs.
seed_data_creation: localStorage.clear() + reload before each test run. Left the Welcome/hello.py file's content mutated by the last test (final content: 'print("fixed")'). No server-side data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New testIDs introduced by this feature set: 'paste-toast' (index.tsx, transient toast after fence strip), 'why-btn' (index.tsx, in the Run BottomSheetModal header — visible ONLY when runOutput.stderr or runOutput.stdout is truthy; icon and label switch on stderr presence), 'apply-fix-btn' (ai.tsx MessageBubble, ONLY on the first code block of assistant messages), 'insert-code-btn' + 'copy-code-btn' (ai.tsx MessageBubble, on every code block). Playwright gotcha: after tapping apply-fix-btn on /ai, the Console BottomSheetModal from index.tsx remains portal-rendered — .click(force=True) may register on the sheet overlay instead of the button. Fallback that works reliably: use `page.mouse.click(x, y)` on the bounding box of the apply-fix-btn. Also, the paste-toast only lives 1.6s, so poll for it every 100ms starting immediately after navigation. The Apply Fix flow can also be exercised end-to-end WITHOUT the live LLM by setting `localStorage.setItem('syntax.pending_replace', '```python\nprint("fixed")\n```')` then navigating to /ai and back — this exercises the useFocusEffect handler, the defensive fence strip and the paste-toast in ~200ms total. Use this pattern to keep tests deterministic.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no defects. All feature acceptance criteria met.
